I want some plants for freshness and aesthetics, but I live in an apartment and haven't owned a plant in a long time. It's usually hot here. Do you guys have any suggestions?
What plants can a beginner use in an apartment?
Cacti! They love the heat (depending on variety) and are nearly impossible to kill. I love plants but I often travel, so I have a few cacti and succulents at home to brighten up the atmosphere.
I've never considered cacti to be good looking. Are there any variants you would suggest?

I really like them, I think they are way cool. If not though, I am sure you can find other easy to take care of beginner plants. How about succulents though? They are way cool and look like a cross between a cacti and a plant.

And I can't recommend any varieties as I don't even know the varieties of the ones I have, sorry.
oooooo, I do like those :). Thank you!
Ferns are always nice. Aloe and spider plants seem to do good in apartments too.

There are some very forgiving Hoyas out there. Getting them to bloom is a different story, but keeping them happy and sustained in an apartment is an easy task for most of the types you find at NA green houses. Hindu rope is a favorite for many. They do fine in low lighting and stay plump as long as you don't let the soil dry out for weeks on end.

I second this. I'm pants with plants, but I've had my Hoya Carnosa for over 10 years now. Mine didn't bloom for the first two years, then it bloomed one year, but not the next, and then it bloomed two years in a row, but not the third.. and now it blooms a bit whenever it feels like it.

Here's a closeup image I took of the flowers. That drop is nectar, or so I believe. It smells really nice. It's a bit sticky too, like syrup, but it mostly stays on the flower. The flowers are very soft, and the middle starshape feels like plastic almost.
